messages.subject: R connection issues with relative path and executable jar
messages.subject_clean: R connection issues with relative path and executable jar
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am writing a `Java` application in IntelliJ IDE. The application uses `Rserve()` to connect to `R` and access scripts. First question is: At the moment, my `R` scripts are directly under my main java project folder. To access a `R` script, I use the following code: 

    RConnection rc1 = new RConnection();
    rc1.assign("parseFile", currentPath.concat("/parseFile.R"));
    rc1.eval("source(parseFile)");

The `currentPath` variable in the code is the absolute path, which I obtain using this:

     final String currentPath = currentRelativePath.toAbsolutePath().toString();

However, I want to make changes in my code and would like to access my `R` scripts using relative path. For this, I created a folder named `rscripts` in the `src` folder and placed my `R` scripts in this folder. I then marked this directory as `Sources root` using the `Mark directory as` option in intelliJ. To access the scripts I made the following changes to the code: 

    rc1.assign("parseFile", "/rscripts/parseFile.R");
    rc1.eval("source(parseFile)");

However, now I get the error:

    org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.RserveException: eval failed, request status: error code: 127

Looking at the error, it seems that `R` script cannot be accessed. 
How should I use relative paths to access the `R` scripts? 

Secondly, I want to deliver my application as a jar file. Should I also bundle `R` with the `jar` file, in case the user does not have R installed on the system? 

Thank you

Best regards,
Purva

messages.body_plain:
The conventional method when bundling external scripts into a jar is to
extract them to temp files, the location and exact name of which will be up
to the JRE.  For example:

final String path;
try (InputStream resource =
Foo.class.getResourceAsStream("/scripts/parseFile.R")) {
    File myFile = File.createTempFile("parseFile", ".R");
    try (FileOutputStream out = new FileOutputStream(myFile)) {
        IOUtils.copy(resource, out);
    }
    path = myFile.getAbsolutePath();
}

Please forgive any syntax or usage errors as I've just written this without
compilation checks or tests.

Relative paths in the absence of some sort of explicit base path are
probably best avoided.

--Steve


--
Steve Kradel
Director, Product Development
Coriell Life Sciences
Camden, New Jersey
856-668-2072

messages.subject: Bad performance with parallel requests
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I think I sent the email to the wrong place, so I am going to resend my
problem, if I am repeating myself, I am sorry.

My case is that I am trying to run a predictive model using R and I
expected getting around ~70reqs/second as normal use case. I will run more
than one machine with this code, but I would like to have a good
performance per machine running the model.

My setup is fairly simple. I have a java front end that will listen to HTTP
calls and forward them to Rserve. The incoming requests are in JSON format
and we send them as they are to the R code. We expect the model to
transform the JSON to proper R structures, crunch the data and then
transformed back to JSON when returning to the java code.

Bellow I show an example on how it looks like.

Code

My code that starts Rserve looks like this:

library(jsonlite)
library(Rserve)

apply_model <- function(input) {

    transformed <- fromJSON(input)

    return(toJSON(transformed));
}
Rserve::run.Rserve(port = 6311, remote=TRUE, auth=FALSE)


The java code that listen to HTTP requests and forwards to RServe. It's a
simple spring boot app.

@RequestMapping(value = "/score",
    method = RequestMethod.POST,
    consumes = MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON_VALUE,
    produces = MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON_VALUE)
public String predict(@RequestBody String input) throws Exception {
    RConnection connection = null;
    try {
        connection = connectionPool.borrowObject();
        connection.assign("input", input);
        return connection.eval("apply_model(input)").toString();
    } finally {
        if (connection != null) {
            connectionPool.returnObject(connection);
        }
    }
}


The connectionPool it's a simple implementation that basically only opens
connections and maintain them open. We are using apache commons pool
library (https://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-pool/). We are setting a
maximum of 20 connections to be opened.

Testing

I am running this in a mac with core i7 with 16gb of memory. It should be
able to handle a lot of requests in parallel fairly easy.

Doing with 5 requests/second I get an average of 13ms to run it.

Increasing to 10req/second increases the average to 21ms.

Increasing to 20req/sec it averages to 33ms.

When I check the CPU usage is under 20% and each R process is taking ~40mb
of memory, not even getting close of my machine being stressed.

   - Can anyone help me understand what's making R increase the timings
   when I increase the number of requests/second?
   - How do you guys handle a lot of requests?
   - Do you always open new connections to RSeve or do you maintain them?
